owner_taxonomy.identity: authentication, authorization, accounts, credentials, access policy, and service principals
owner_taxonomy.storage: blobs, files, snapshots, retention, object data, and storage access
owner_taxonomy.compute: virtual machines, containers, hosts, scheduling, autoscale, CPU, and memory

findings.description: Conditional access policy excludes a break-glass group.
Blob container permits anonymous object reads.
VM scale set health probes use the wrong port.
Topic authorization grants publish access to a guest tenant.
MFA registration bypass remains enabled for contractors.
Storage account keys have not rotated within policy.
Hypervisor host is missing the required isolation patch.
Queue lock timeout is shorter than handler execution time.
Guest account review is overdue.
Lifecycle policy moves active blobs to archive.
Autoscale minimum keeps idle compute nodes running.
Subscription retry delay causes delivery backlog.
App registration retains an unused privileged scope.
File share permits legacy unauthenticated protocol access.
Container host exposes the runtime socket.
Event stream checkpointing is disabled.
OAuth refresh tokens remain valid after the user account is disabled.
A public snapshot grants anonymous read access to archived objects.
The autoscaler oscillates because CPU metrics arrive several minutes late.
Dead-letter messages disappear after a topic failover.
A service principal keeps an administrator role after credential rotation.
Object version retention deletes the copy protected by legal hold.
The VM scheduler pins burst workloads to one physical node.
Queue subscription retries deliver duplicate messages.
